checklist.step: Kick off the annual B-13 self-assessment cycle and pull the prior-year baseline
actions: Open the GRC platform's B-13 self-assessment module and clone the prior fiscal year's completed assessment as the current-year baseline.
Update the assessment header with the current fiscal year, target certification date (fiscal year end + 180 days) and the assigned domain owners.
Notify domain owners (IT Security Manager, Operational Resilience Lead, Third-Party Risk Manager) via the GRC platform's task assignment that the cycle is open.
Attach the current OSFI Guideline B-13 (Technology and Cyber Risk Management) PDF to the assessment record as the scoring reference.
checklist.done: the current-year assessment shell exists in the GRC platform with domain owners assigned and the B-13 reference attached.

checklist.step: Refresh the control inventory against the current B-13 domains
actions: In the GRC platform, open the control library filtered to the five B-13 domains (Governance & Risk Management, Technology Operations, Technology Resilience, Cyber Security, Third-Party Technology/Cyber Risk).
Compare each control's description and owner against the current guideline text; retire controls tied to withdrawn requirements and add controls for any new sub-domain.
Map each control to at least one control owner in the GRC platform's RACI field.
Flag orphaned controls (no owner) to the CISO for assignment before scoring opens.
checklist.done: every control in the library is mapped one-to-one to a current B-13 domain/sub-domain and has an assigned owner.

checklist.step: Score each domain and sub-domain against the maturity scale
actions: For each control, request the current design and operating-effectiveness rating from its owner using the GRC platform's rating scale (Not in Place / Partially in Place / In Place / Optimized).
Attach the owner's supporting evidence link (policy, scan report, ticket) to each rating.
Roll sub-domain scores up to a domain-level score using the GRC platform's weighted rollup.
Where a domain scores below 'In Place', open a gap record referencing the specific control(s) driving the score.
checklist.done: every domain has a rolled-up score with owner-attested, evidence-linked ratings underneath it.

checklist.step: Gather control evidence from security and IT operations tooling
actions: Pull the current CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint coverage report and the Qualys / Tenable vulnerability scan summary for the reporting period.
Export the SIEM/SOAR incident and alert-response metrics covering mean time to detect and mean time to respond.
Pull access review completion evidence from the IAM platform (SailPoint/Okta/Azure AD).
Attach each extract to the corresponding control in the GRC platform with the extraction date.
checklist.done: every technical control cites a dated extract from the source security tool, not a narrative claim.

checklist.step: Identify gaps and open remediation items
actions: Review the gap records raised during scoring and confirm each cites the specific control, the target maturity level and the current level.
Prioritize gaps using the enterprise risk taxonomy (High/Medium/Low) based on the CRO's risk appetite thresholds.
Open a remediation item per gap in the GRC platform's issue module, linked back to the control and domain.
checklist.done: every sub-target domain has a prioritized, control-linked remediation item open in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Draft remediation plans with owners and target dates
actions: For each remediation item, assign an accountable owner from the domain team and a target close date that lands before the certification submission date.
Where a remediation cannot close before filing, draft a compensating-control statement and an interim risk acceptance for CRO sign-off.
Load target dates into the GRC platform's remediation tracker with automated overdue alerts.
checklist.done: every remediation item has an owner, a target date, and — where it will not close in time — a CRO-ready risk acceptance draft.

checklist.step: Validate evidence with control owners before compiling the report
actions: Walk each domain owner through their scored controls and attached evidence in a validation session.
Correct any rating where the evidence does not support the score and re-date the rating.
Lock the assessment record in the GRC platform once the owner confirms accuracy, which timestamps the final scores.
checklist.done: every domain owner has confirmed their scores and evidence, and the assessment record is locked.

checklist.step: Compile the self-assessment summary report
actions: Export the locked assessment from the GRC platform into the self-assessment summary template covering domain scores, key gaps, remediation status and residual risk.
Add the year-over-year trend comparison against the prior certification.
Route the draft to the Chief Risk Officer and Operational Resilience Lead for technical accuracy review.
checklist.done: a complete draft summary report exists with scores, gaps, remediation status and trend, reviewed by CRO and Operational Resilience Lead.

checklist.step: Present the assessment to the Chief Risk Officer for review
actions: Walk the CRO through domain scores, open remediation items and any proposed risk acceptances.
Capture the CRO's questions and required changes directly on the summary report.
Obtain the CRO's written endorsement to proceed to Board Risk Committee.
checklist.done: the CRO has reviewed the summary and given written endorsement to advance it to the Board Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Present to the Board Risk Committee for endorsement
actions: Add the self-assessment summary as an agenda item on the board portal for the next Board Risk Committee meeting.
Present domain scores, key gaps, remediation plans and any risk acceptances requiring committee approval.
Record the committee's endorsement, any conditions, and required follow-ups in the board portal's minutes.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee's endorsement (or conditions) is recorded in the board portal minutes.

checklist.step: Incorporate Board feedback and finalize the assessment
actions: Update the summary report and any risk acceptance language per the committee's recorded conditions.
Re-circulate the finalized version to the CRO for final sign-off.
Lock the finalized version as the certification support package in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: the finalized package reflects all Board conditions and carries CRO final sign-off.

checklist.step: Draft and sign the certification letter
actions: Draft the certification letter attesting to the entity's compliance status against B-13, referencing the finalized self-assessment package.
Include named exceptions and their remediation timelines rather than omitting them.
Sign the certification and route to the Chief Risk Officer for countersignature.
checklist.done: the certification letter is drafted, exceptions are named, and both CISO and CRO signatures are on file.

checklist.step: Submit the certification through the OSFI Regulatory Reporting System
actions: Log in to OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System (RRS) and open the current filing period's technology & cyber risk certification submission.
Upload the signed certification letter and the self-assessment summary as supporting attachments.
Complete the RRS submission metadata (institution code, fiscal year end, filer contact) and submit before the 180-day deadline.
Save the RRS confirmation number and submission timestamp to the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the certification is submitted in RRS before the 180-day deadline with a saved confirmation number.

checklist.step: Confirm submission receipt and log the confirmation
actions: Check the RRS submission status shows 'Received' or 'Accepted' rather than 'Pending' or 'Rejected'.
If rejected, read the RRS error detail, correct the submission and resubmit the same business day.
Log the confirmation number, submission date and status in the regulatory filing/issue tracker against this obligation.
checklist.done: the RRS status shows accepted and the confirmation is logged in the filing tracker.

checklist.step: Retain the certification evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the locked self-assessment package, certification letter, Board minutes and RRS confirmation into the compliance evidence repository under the current fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index shows the record searchable by fiscal year and RRS confirmation number.
checklist.done: the full certification record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by fiscal year and confirmation number.

testing.step: Build the population of B-13 domains and controls scored in the current certification
actions: Export from the GRC platform every domain, sub-domain and control scored in the current-year self-assessment.
Reconcile the exported control count to the control library's active-control count for the period.
Resolve any discrepancy with the Security GRC Analyst before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the active control library and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the certification submission to the finalized assessment package
actions: Compare the certification letter's attested scope and exceptions to the locked self-assessment package.
Confirm the RRS submission attachments match the Board-endorsed final version exactly.
List any mismatch (score changed post-Board endorsement without re-approval) as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the RRS submission is confirmed identical to the Board-endorsed package or discrepancies are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of domains scoring below 'In Place'.
Take a random sample of 10 controls from domains scoring 'In Place' or 'Optimized', seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every below-target domain.

testing.step: Re-perform the control rating for each sampled control
actions: Open the evidence attached to each sampled control in the GRC platform and independently assess whether it supports the recorded rating.
Reach an independent maturity rating without viewing the owner's conclusion first.
Compare to the recorded rating; any difference of more than one maturity level is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled control has an independent re-performed rating and a documented comparison.

testing.step: Verify remediation plans and risk acceptances for sampled gaps
actions: For each sampled control with an open gap, confirm a remediation item exists with an owner and target date.
For any gap open past its certification-cycle target, confirm a CRO-signed risk acceptance exists.
Flag any gap with neither a remediation plan nor a risk acceptance.
testing.done: every sampled gap has a remediation plan or a signed risk acceptance, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Confirm Board Risk Committee endorsement occurred before filing
actions: Pull the Board Risk Committee minutes from the board portal for the meeting where the assessment was presented.
Confirm the endorsement date precedes the RRS submission date.
Confirm any committee conditions are reflected in the finalized package.
testing.done: Board endorsement is confirmed to pre-date the filing and conditions are reflected in the final package.

testing.step: Trace the RRS filing to a valid, on-time submission
actions: Open OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System and pull the submission record using the saved confirmation number.
Confirm the submission timestamp is on or before fiscal year end + 180 days.
Confirm the attached certification letter matches the signed copy in the evidence repository.
Capture the RRS submission detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: the RRS record confirms an on-time, matching submission, captured as evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the 180-day deadline and confirm the reminder schedule fired
actions: Recompute the 180-day deadline from the fiscal year end date independently.
Compare to the recorded target certification date on the assessment record.
Confirm the GRC platform's T-120/T-60/T-30 alerts fired and were acted on, using the platform's notification log.
testing.done: the recomputed deadline matches the tracked date and the reminder log shows all three alerts fired.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the control, domain, and what was missed.
Assign a root cause (evidence gap, rating override, missed reminder, late Board slot) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open exceptions into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance late-filing threshold and the rating-accuracy threshold.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who scored none of the sampled controls, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate exists, reported to the Board Risk Committee.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns third-party risk oversight for critical service providers; escalation to Third-Party Risk Manager and Chief Risk Officer

checklist.step: Tier every third-party relationship by criticality
actions: Export the full vendor list from the GRC platform's vendor risk register.
Score each vendor against the criticality framework (impact of failure, data sensitivity, substitutability, regulatory relevance) to classify Critical, Material or Standard.
Confirm Critical and Material classifications with the Third-Party Risk Manager and the business owner.
Update the criticality tier field on each vendor record in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every active vendor carries a confirmed criticality tier in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Run due diligence before onboarding any new critical or material vendor
actions: Send the vendor the due-diligence questionnaire covering financial soundness, security posture, business continuity capability, sub-contracting and data location.
Request the vendor's SOC 2 Type II report (or equivalent) and independent penetration test summary.
Score the responses against the GRC platform's risk criteria and record the resulting risk rating.
Escalate any unacceptable rating to the Chief Risk Officer before contracting proceeds.
checklist.done: a completed, scored due-diligence file exists for the vendor before any contract is signed.

checklist.step: Negotiate the required B-10 contractual provisions
actions: Pull the B-10 contract clause checklist from the GRC platform (service levels, security requirements, sub-contracting consent, business continuity, audit and OSFI access rights, data location, termination/exit).
Mark each clause present/absent/negotiated on the draft agreement and route gaps to Legal Counsel for redline.
Confirm the OSFI regulator-access clause explicitly grants OSFI the right to examine the vendor and its records.
File the signed agreement in the contract lifecycle management repository, tagged with the vendor's criticality tier.
checklist.done: the executed contract carries every required B-10 clause, verified against the checklist and filed in the CLM repository.

checklist.step: Register the vendor and link it to the process and application it supports
actions: Create or update the vendor record in the GRC platform with legal entity name, service description, criticality tier and contract reference.
Link the vendor record to the ProcessNode(s) and Application(s) it services in the operating model.
Assign a named internal relationship owner and a named Third-Party Risk Manager contact.
checklist.done: the vendor record is complete, linked to its supported process/application, and carries named owners.

checklist.step: Confirm sub-contractor (fourth-party) visibility
actions: Request the vendor's current sub-contractor list for any function material to the service.
Confirm the contract's sub-contracting clause requires notice before any new sub-contractor is engaged.
Assess each disclosed sub-contractor's criticality using the same tiering framework and record it against the parent vendor.
checklist.done: the vendor's sub-contractor list is on file, tiered, and the notice-of-change clause is confirmed active.

checklist.step: Set the ongoing monitoring cadence
actions: Set the GRC platform's monitoring cadence per criticality tier — quarterly for Critical, semi-annual for Material.
Configure monitoring scope: SLA performance, security incident notifications, financial health checks and control attestations.
Assign the relationship owner as the monitoring task recipient in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every vendor has a cadence, scope and owner configured in the GRC platform's monitoring module.

checklist.step: Collect and review the vendor's periodic control attestations
actions: Request the vendor's current SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test summary and BCP test results per the monitoring cadence.
Review the report for qualified opinions or control exceptions relevant to the services provided.
Log the review outcome and any follow-up items in the GRC platform against the vendor record.
checklist.done: the current-period attestation is reviewed, logged, and any exception has a follow-up item.

checklist.step: Run the annual reassessment for every critical/material vendor
actions: Re-issue the due-diligence questionnaire and re-score the vendor's risk rating against current criteria.
Compare the new rating to the prior year's and investigate any material deterioration with the vendor.
Update the vendor's risk rating and reassessment date in the GRC platform before the anniversary deadline.
checklist.done: the vendor's reassessment is complete, scored and dated in the GRC platform before its anniversary.

checklist.step: Test incident notification and escalation readiness
actions: Confirm the contract's incident notification clause specifies the notification window (e.g., within 24-72 hours of a material incident).
Review the vendor's incident history for the period and confirm each notification met the contractual window.
Log any missed or late notification as a vendor performance exception in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: notification timeliness is checked against the contractual window for every incident in the period.

checklist.step: Verify business continuity and exit/contingency planning
actions: Request the vendor's current business continuity plan and most recent test results for the service provided.
Confirm the internal exit plan for this vendor names an alternate provider or in-house fallback and an estimated transition timeline.
Update the exit plan document with current vendor-specific details and file it alongside the vendor record.
checklist.done: current BCP test evidence and an up-to-date, vendor-specific exit plan are on file.

checklist.step: Assess concentration risk across the critical vendor portfolio
actions: Aggregate critical vendors by underlying cloud/data-center provider and by geography in the GRC platform's concentration report.
Flag any single point of failure serving multiple critical processes.
Present concentration findings to the Chief Risk Officer with any recommended diversification action.
checklist.done: a current concentration report exists and any single point of failure is flagged to the CRO.

checklist.step: Escalate unresolved critical-vendor risk findings
actions: Review any vendor risk rating downgraded to unacceptable or any unresolved clause gap past 90 days.
Decide remediation, contract renegotiation or vendor exit, and record the decision with a target date.
Report material third-party risk decisions to the Board Risk Committee via the board portal.
checklist.done: every unresolved critical finding has an owned decision recorded and reported to the Board Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Update the vendor risk register status
actions: Set each vendor's GRC platform status to Current, Reassessment Due, or Remediation In Progress based on this cycle's outcome.
Attach the completed due-diligence file, clause checklist and monitoring reports as the status evidence.
Confirm the relationship owner has acknowledged the updated status.
checklist.done: every vendor record shows a current status backed by attached evidence, acknowledged by the relationship owner.

checklist.step: Log any exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any vendor missing a required clause, an overdue reassessment, or a failed monitoring check.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Track the exception to closure in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date logged.

checklist.step: Retain the vendor oversight evidence
actions: Move the due-diligence file, signed contract, clause checklist and monitoring reports into the compliance evidence repository under the vendor name.
Apply the 7-year-from-termination retention label.
Confirm the repository index shows the record searchable by vendor name and criticality tier.
checklist.done: the vendor oversight record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by vendor name.

testing.step: Build the population of critical and material vendors
actions: Export every vendor tiered Critical or Material from the GRC platform's vendor risk register.
Reconcile the count to the contract lifecycle management repository's active-contract count for the same population.
Resolve any discrepancy with the Vendor Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to active contracts and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each vendor to a signed, on-file contract
actions: Match each population vendor to a signed agreement in the contract lifecycle management repository.
Confirm the contract is current (not expired) and covers the services actually in use.
List any vendor without a matching current contract as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every population vendor matches a current signed contract or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of Critical-tier vendors.
Take a random sample of 10 Material-tier vendors, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible and covers 100% of Critical vendors.

testing.step: Re-check the contract for required B-10 clauses
actions: Open each sampled vendor's contract in the contract lifecycle management repository.
Independently check for the service-level, security, sub-contracting, business continuity, audit/OSFI-access, data-location and exit clauses without viewing the checklist result first.
Compare to the recorded clause checklist; any missing clause not previously flagged is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled contract has an independent clause check with a documented comparison to the checklist.

testing.step: Verify due diligence and reassessment evidence
actions: Pull the due-diligence file and most recent reassessment for each sampled vendor.
Confirm the reassessment date is within the required cadence for the vendor's criticality tier.
Confirm the SOC 2 / penetration test evidence cited is dated within the current review period.
testing.done: each sampled vendor's due diligence and reassessment timing is confirmed current or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Test incident notification compliance
actions: Pull the vendor's incident log for the period from the GRC platform.
For each incident, compare the notification timestamp to the contractual notification window.
Flag any notification outside the contractual window.
testing.done: every incident in the sample period is checked against the contractual notification window.

testing.step: Verify exit/contingency plan currency
actions: Open the exit plan for each sampled critical vendor and confirm it names a current alternate provider or fallback.
Confirm the plan was reviewed or updated within the last 12 months.
Flag any stale or generic exit plan lacking vendor-specific detail.
testing.done: each sampled critical vendor's exit plan is confirmed current and vendor-specific, or flagged.

testing.step: Recompute concentration risk exposure
actions: Independently aggregate sampled critical vendors by underlying infrastructure provider and geography.
Compare the recomputed concentration to the Third-Party Risk Manager's reported concentration findings.
Flag any single point of failure omitted from the original report.
testing.done: recomputed concentration matches the reported findings or the difference is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the vendor, clause or control missed.
Assign a root cause (contract drafting gap, missed cadence, stale exit plan) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open exceptions into next cycle's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance missing-clause threshold.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled due diligence, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate exists, reported to the Board Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Open the statutory close calendar for the period
actions: Open the financial close calendar in the ERP system and confirm the quarterly (45-day) or annual (90-day) filing deadline is loaded from period end.
Assign close tasks to the Statutory Reporting Manager, Senior Accountant and Appointed Actuary with due dates backed off the filing deadline.
Confirm prior-period open items are cleared before the new cycle opens.
checklist.done: the close calendar is loaded with deadline-backed task dates and assigned owners.

checklist.step: Extract and lock the statutory trial balance
actions: In the ERP/General ledger system, run the trial balance extract for the statutory legal entity as of period end.
Reconcile the extract total to the GL control account and resolve any out-of-balance condition before proceeding.
Lock the trial balance snapshot and timestamp it in the financial reporting repository.
checklist.done: a reconciled, locked trial balance snapshot exists for the period.

checklist.step: Post statutory adjusting entries
actions: Identify GAAP-to-statutory differences (non-admitted assets, statutory reserve basis, deferred tax) using the prior-period adjustment template.
Post each adjusting entry in the ERP system with a memo citing the statutory basis for the adjustment.
Route entries above the materiality threshold to the Controller for pre-posting approval.
checklist.done: all statutory adjusting entries are posted, referenced to their basis, and material entries carry Controller approval.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial reserve figures and tie them to the general ledger
actions: Request the current-period statutory reserve summary from the Appointed Actuary, by line of business and reserve category.
Compare the actuarial summary total to the reserve liability balance in the trial balance.
Resolve any difference with the Appointed Actuary and document the resolution before proceeding.

checklist.step: Confirm the external auditor engagement and independence
actions: Confirm the Audit Committee's re-appointment (or new appointment) of the external audit firm for the current fiscal year.
Obtain the auditor's written independence confirmation covering non-audit services performed in the period.
Sign the engagement letter and file it in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed engagement letter and independence confirmation are on file before fieldwork begins.

checklist.step: Build and issue the PBC (prepared-by-client) list
actions: Pull the current-year PBC list template from AuditBoard and update it with the auditor's requested items.
Assign each PBC item to a preparer with a due date backed off the fieldwork start date.
Distribute the list and confirm receipt with each preparer.
checklist.done: a complete PBC list with assigned owners and due dates is issued in AuditBoard.

checklist.step: Fulfill each PBC deliverable
actions: Extract the requested support from the ERP general ledger, financial reporting repository or relevant sub-ledger.
Upload each deliverable to AuditBoard against its PBC line item before the due date.
Mark each item Ready for Review once uploaded and tie to source confirmed.
checklist.done: every PBC item is uploaded and marked ready before its due date, or flagged late with a reason.

checklist.step: Coordinate audit fieldwork logistics
actions: Schedule fieldwork access (system access, workspace, interview slots with process owners) with the auditor's engagement team.
Set up read-only auditor access to the ERP system and AuditBoard for the fieldwork period.
Track daily fieldwork status against the audit project plan.
checklist.done: fieldwork access is provisioned and status is tracked daily against the plan.

checklist.step: Support the auditor's substantive testing requests
actions: Respond to auditor sample requests by pulling the specific transaction or schedule detail requested.
Log each auditor request and its fulfillment date in AuditBoard.
Escalate any request the business cannot fulfill within the agreed turnaround to the Controller.
checklist.done: every auditor request is logged with a fulfillment date, and unmet requests are escalated.

checklist.step: Track and triage audit findings as they are raised
actions: Log each finding raised by the auditor in AuditBoard with its classification (control deficiency, significant deficiency, material weakness).
Assign an owner and a target response date to each finding.
Brief the Chief Financial Officer weekly during fieldwork on open findings.
checklist.done: every finding is logged, classified, owned and reported weekly.

checklist.step: Draft management responses to audit findings
actions: For each finding, draft the root cause and remediation plan in AuditBoard.
Route significant deficiency and material weakness responses to the Chief Financial Officer for review before submission to the auditor.
Submit the response to the auditor within the agreed turnaround.
checklist.done: every finding has a management response drafted, CFO-reviewed where required, and submitted on time.

checklist.step: Obtain the management representation letter sign-off
actions: Review the auditor's draft management representation letter for accuracy against the final financial statements.
Sign the representation letter dated as close to the opinion date as the audit plan requires.
File the signed letter in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed, correctly dated management representation letter is on file.

checklist.step: Present the audit results to the Audit Committee
actions: Prepare the Audit Committee presentation summarizing the audit scope, key findings and management responses.
Present via the board portal at the pre-filing Audit Committee meeting.
Record the committee's approval to proceed to opinion issuance in the meeting minutes.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee's approval is recorded in the board portal minutes before the opinion is issued.

checklist.step: Receive and review the auditor's opinion
actions: Receive the draft audit opinion and confirm the opinion type (unqualified/qualified) and scope match the engagement letter.
Confirm every material weakness or significant deficiency disclosed in the opinion has a corresponding management response on file.
Route the final opinion to the Chief Financial Officer for acceptance.
checklist.done: the opinion is reviewed, matched against management responses, and accepted by the CFO.

checklist.step: Finalize the audited financial statements
actions: Incorporate the signed audit opinion into the final audited financial statement package.
Confirm the statements reflect any final audit adjustments agreed during fieldwork.
Generate the final package for filing.
checklist.done: the final audited statement package includes the signed opinion and all agreed adjustments.

checklist.step: File the audited financial statements with the regulator
actions: Upload the final audited statement package to OSFI's Regulatory Reporting System (and NAIC iSite+ where applicable for US-licensed business).
Complete the submission metadata and submit before the regulatory filing deadline.
Save the confirmation number and timestamp.
checklist.done: the audited statements are filed before the deadline with a saved confirmation number.

checklist.step: Confirm filing acceptance
actions: Check the filing system status shows Accepted rather than Pending or Rejected.
If rejected, correct and resubmit the same business day.
Log the confirmation in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
checklist.done: the filing status shows accepted and is logged in the tracker.

checklist.step: Log any audit coordination exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any PBC item delivered late or any finding without a timely management response.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Track the exception to closure in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date logged.

checklist.step: Retain the audit evidence
actions: Move the PBC deliverables, findings log, management representation letter and signed opinion into the compliance evidence repository under the fiscal year.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Confirm the repository index shows the record searchable by fiscal year and auditor engagement.
checklist.done: the audit coordination record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by fiscal year.

testing.step: Build the population of PBC items and audit findings
actions: Export the full PBC list and findings log from AuditBoard for the current audit cycle.
Reconcile the PBC count to the auditor's original request list.
Resolve any discrepancy with the Controller before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the auditor's request list and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile PBC delivery dates to due dates
actions: Compare each PBC item's AuditBoard upload timestamp to its assigned due date.
List any item delivered after its due date without a documented extension as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every PBC item's timeliness is confirmed or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of significant deficiency and material weakness findings.
Take a random sample of 10 remaining PBC items, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all significant findings.

testing.step: Re-verify sampled PBC deliverables tie to source
actions: Independently trace each sampled PBC deliverable back to the ERP general ledger or source system.
Confirm the uploaded document matches the source without alteration.
Flag any deliverable that does not tie to source.
testing.done: each sampled PBC deliverable is independently traced to source and confirmed accurate.

testing.step: Verify management responses to sampled findings
actions: Pull the management response for each sampled significant/material finding.
Confirm the response includes a root cause, an owner and a target date.
Confirm CFO review is on file where required.
testing.done: every sampled finding has a complete, CFO-reviewed management response, or the gap is flagged.

testing.step: Confirm the management representation letter and Audit Committee approval
actions: Pull the signed management representation letter and confirm its date relative to the opinion date.
Pull the Audit Committee minutes confirming approval to proceed to opinion issuance.
Confirm the approval date precedes the filing date.
testing.done: the representation letter and committee approval are confirmed present and correctly sequenced.

testing.step: Trace the filing to a valid, on-time submission
actions: Pull the filing confirmation record for the audited statements using the saved confirmation number.
Confirm the submission timestamp is on or before the regulatory deadline.
Capture the confirmation screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: the filing record confirms an on-time submission, captured as evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline and confirm reminders fired
actions: Recompute the audited-statement filing deadline independently from fiscal year end.
Compare to the tracked deadline in the audit project plan.
Confirm the T-60/T-30/T-10 alerts fired, using the plan's notification log.
testing.done: the recomputed deadline matches the tracked date and reminders are confirmed fired.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the PBC item or finding and what was missed.
Assign a root cause (late data pull, unresponsive process owner, missed fieldwork slot) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open exceptions into next year's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance late-filing and unresolved-finding thresholds.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who is independent of the audit coordination team, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate exists, reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Establish the master filing calendar structure
actions: Set up the master filing calendar in the GRC platform with one row per jurisdiction/filing-type/period combination.
Define required fields: jurisdiction, filing type, statutory deadline, internal readiness date, owner, status, confirmation number.
Load the current-year OSFI, NAIC and state deadlines from each regulator's published schedule.
checklist.done: the calendar is structured with all required fields and populated with current-year deadlines.

checklist.step: Monitor jurisdictions for filing-calendar or deadline changes
actions: Subscribe to OSFI, NAIC and each active state's regulatory bulletin distribution.
Review each bulletin for filing-calendar changes and log any change on the calendar update log.
Update the master calendar within 5 business days of a published change.
checklist.done: the master calendar reflects every published deadline change within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Intake new filing obligations
actions: When a new product line, jurisdiction or line of business is added, request the applicable filing requirements from Regulatory Counsel.
Add the new obligation to the master calendar with its first applicable deadline.
Assign an owner and readiness date for the new obligation.
checklist.done: every new obligation is added to the calendar with an owner before its first deadline.

checklist.step: Verify the calendar against each regulator's published schedule quarterly
actions: Pull the current NAIC filing calendar, OSFI reporting instructions schedule and each state's published deadlines.
Compare line-by-line to the master calendar and correct any discrepancy.
Document the verification date and source on the calendar record.
checklist.done: the calendar is verified against regulator sources quarterly with a documented verification date.

checklist.step: Track readiness status leading into each deadline
actions: Review the calendar weekly for entries within 30 days of their deadline.
Confirm each entry's status (Not Started/In Progress/Ready/Submitted) is current based on direct check-in with the preparer.
Escalate any entry stuck below Ready status past its internal readiness date.
checklist.done: every near-term entry's status is current and any stuck entry is escalated.

checklist.step: Capture timeliness evidence for every completed filing
actions: For each submitted filing, capture the portal confirmation screen and confirmation number.
Link the evidence to the calendar entry in the GRC platform.
Confirm the submission timestamp is recorded alongside the statutory deadline for direct comparison.
checklist.done: every completed filing's calendar entry links to a captured confirmation with timestamp.

checklist.step: Flag and escalate any missed deadline immediately
actions: Run a daily check for any calendar entry past its statutory deadline without a Submitted status.
Escalate any missed deadline to the Chief Financial Officer and Regulatory Counsel the same business day.
Open a late-filing exception record and begin the self-report assessment where required by the jurisdiction.
checklist.done: any missed deadline is escalated the same business day with an open exception record.

checklist.step: Reconcile the calendar to actual filings monthly
actions: Compare the month's Submitted-status entries to the actual confirmation numbers on file.
Compare the month's due entries to filings actually made, regardless of calendar status, to catch off-calendar filings.
Correct any calendar/reality mismatch and document the correction.
checklist.done: the calendar reconciles to actual filing activity each month, with corrections documented.

checklist.step: Review the calendar for completeness at each quarter end
actions: Confirm every jurisdiction the company is licensed or registered in has at least the base set of expected filing types represented on the calendar.
Cross-check the licensed-jurisdiction list from the producer/entity licensing system against the calendar's jurisdiction list.
Add any missing jurisdiction/filing-type combination immediately.
checklist.done: the calendar covers every licensed jurisdiction's expected filing types, confirmed each quarter.

checklist.step: Audit a sample of calendar entries for evidence completeness
actions: Pull a monthly sample of completed entries and confirm each has linked confirmation evidence and a timestamp.
Correct any entry missing evidence by retrieving the confirmation from the source portal.
Log any entry that cannot be evidenced as an exception.
checklist.done: the monthly sample confirms evidence completeness, with any gap logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Present the calendar status to leadership periodically
actions: Prepare a calendar status summary (upcoming 90-day deadlines, at-risk entries, missed filings) for the Controller and CFO.
Present the summary at the regular compliance/regulatory reporting review meeting.
Record any leadership direction on at-risk items in the meeting notes.
checklist.done: a calendar status summary is presented periodically and leadership direction is recorded.

checklist.step: Update procedure documentation when the process changes
actions: Review the Filing Calendar Governance Procedure annually or when a material process change occurs.
Update the procedure and route to the Chief Financial Officer for re-approval.
Communicate procedure changes to all calendar owners.
checklist.done: the procedure is current, CFO-approved, and communicated to owners.

checklist.step: Perform the annual full calendar audit
actions: Once per year, verify every active calendar entry against its regulator's current published schedule end-to-end.
Confirm every completed filing in the year has linked timeliness evidence.
Document the audit outcome and any corrections made.
checklist.done: a documented annual audit confirms full calendar accuracy and evidence completeness.

checklist.step: Log any calendar exceptions with disposition
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any stale deadline, missing evidence or missed filing found during monitoring.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Track the exception to closure in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date logged.

checklist.step: Retain the calendar and evidence trail
actions: Snapshot the master calendar quarterly and store it in the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label to each snapshot and linked evidence.
Confirm the repository index shows records searchable by jurisdiction and filing period.
checklist.done: quarterly calendar snapshots and linked evidence are filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of completed filings in the test period
actions: Export from the GRC platform every calendar entry marked Submitted in the quarter.
Reconcile the count to the compliance evidence repository's confirmation records for the same period.
Resolve any discrepancy with the Regulatory Reporting Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the evidence repository and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the calendar to the licensed-jurisdiction list
actions: Compare the calendar's jurisdiction list to the current licensed/registered jurisdiction list from the producer/entity licensing system.
List any licensed jurisdiction missing from the calendar as an automatic exception.
testing.done: the calendar's jurisdiction coverage is confirmed complete or gaps are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of any jurisdiction with a filing-calendar change logged in the period.
Take a random sample of 15 remaining completed filings, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every jurisdiction with a logged change.

testing.step: Re-verify timeliness evidence for each sampled filing
actions: Open the linked confirmation evidence for each sampled entry and independently read the submission timestamp.
Compare to the statutory deadline recorded on the calendar entry.
Flag any entry where the evidence does not support an on-time submission.
testing.done: each sampled entry's timeliness is independently confirmed from evidence, or flagged.

testing.step: Re-verify the deadline against the regulator's current published schedule
actions: For each sampled entry, independently pull the regulator's current published deadline for that filing type and period.
Compare to the deadline recorded on the calendar.
Flag any stale or incorrect deadline.
testing.done: each sampled deadline is independently confirmed against the regulator's source, or flagged.

testing.step: Verify reminder alerts fired for sampled entries
actions: Pull the GRC platform's notification log for each sampled entry.
Confirm the T-30/T-15/T-5/T-1 alerts fired as configured.
Flag any entry with a missing or unfired alert.
testing.done: reminder firing is confirmed for every sampled entry, or flagged.

testing.step: Trace missed-deadline entries to a completed escalation
actions: Pull every calendar entry flagged as a missed deadline in the period.
Confirm each has a same-day escalation record and, where applicable, a completed self-report assessment.
Flag any missed deadline without a completed escalation trail.
testing.done: every missed-deadline entry traces to a complete escalation record, or is flagged.

testing.step: Recompute the calendar's coverage completeness
actions: Independently list the expected filing types for a sample of 5 jurisdictions based on their current regulator instructions.
Compare to what the calendar actually tracks for those jurisdictions.
Flag any expected filing type missing from the calendar.
testing.done: coverage completeness is independently confirmed for the sampled jurisdictions, or gaps are flagged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the jurisdiction, entry and what was missed.
Assign a root cause (missed bulletin, stale deadline, evidence not captured) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance missing-evidence and stale-deadline thresholds.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who does not maintain the calendar, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate exists, reported to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Identify and confirm the list of critical operations
actions: Pull the current critical-operations list from the GRC platform's business impact analysis module.
Validate the list with the Chief Risk Officer against the enterprise's severe-but-plausible disruption scenarios.
Update the list for any new or retired critical operation and record the change date.
checklist.done: a current, CRO-validated critical-operations list exists in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Set or re-validate the impact tolerance for each critical operation
actions: For each critical operation, confirm the maximum tolerable disruption (time, data loss, service level) with the accountable business owner.
Compare the current impact tolerance to last year's and document any change with rationale.
Record the validated impact tolerance in the GRC platform against the operation.
checklist.done: every critical operation has a current, owner-confirmed impact tolerance recorded.

checklist.step: Author or update the business continuity plan for each critical operation
actions: Draft or revise the plan covering recovery strategy, recovery time/point objectives, alternate site/process, and dependency mapping (people, systems, third parties).
Cross-reference the plan to the operation's linked applications and the third-party vendors supporting it.
Route the draft to the operation's business owner for review and sign-off.
checklist.done: each critical operation has a current, owner-reviewed plan covering recovery strategy and dependencies.

checklist.step: Author or update the disaster recovery runbook for supporting systems
actions: For each critical operation's supporting application, confirm or update the DR runbook in the ITSM platform covering failover steps, RTO/RPO and rollback.
Confirm the runbook names the current infrastructure/cloud environment and recovery site.
Link the runbook to the corresponding business continuity plan in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: each supporting application has a current, linked DR runbook.

checklist.step: Schedule the annual scenario test calendar
actions: Build the test calendar in the GRC platform covering tabletop exercises, technical failover tests and full-scale scenario simulations for the year.
Assign a test type appropriate to the operation's criticality tier — full-scale for the highest tier, tabletop as a minimum for lower tiers.
Confirm every critical operation is scheduled for at least one test within the fiscal year.
checklist.done: a complete test calendar exists covering every critical operation at least once in the year.

checklist.step: Conduct the scenario test
actions: Execute the scheduled test per its script — invoke the plan, simulate the disruption scenario, and record actual recovery time/data loss achieved.
Capture participant attendance, decisions made, and any deviation from the documented plan during the test.
Log raw test results (times, issues encountered) in the GRC platform immediately after the test.
checklist.done: the test is executed per script with raw results captured in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Assess the test result against the impact tolerance
actions: Compare the actual recovery time/data loss achieved during the test to the operation's validated impact tolerance.
Classify the result as Met, Degraded or Failed.
Record the classification and supporting rationale on the test record.
checklist.done: every test carries a documented Met/Degraded/Failed classification against the impact tolerance.

checklist.step: Write the after-action report and identify gaps
actions: Document what worked, what failed, and root causes for any Degraded or Failed result in the after-action report.
List specific plan or runbook gaps the test exposed.
Attach the after-action report to the plan record in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: an after-action report with root causes and identified gaps is attached to the plan record.

checklist.step: Open and track remediation items for identified gaps
actions: Open a remediation item per gap in the GRC platform, with an owner and a target close date.
For any Failed result, require the remediation plan and interim risk acceptance to be reviewed by the Chief Risk Officer.
Track remediation items to closure and re-test the specific gap where feasible.
checklist.done: every identified gap has an owned, dated remediation item, and Failed results carry CRO review.

checklist.step: Update the plan and runbook based on test findings
actions: Revise the business continuity plan and DR runbook to close the identified gaps.
Route the revised documents to the business owner for re-approval.
Version the updated documents in the GRC platform with a change log entry.
checklist.done: the plan and runbook are revised, re-approved and version-controlled with a change log.

checklist.step: Perform the annual plan review even where no test gap was found
actions: For every critical operation, confirm the plan has been reviewed within the last 12 months regardless of test outcome.
Update the plan for any organizational, system or vendor change since the last review.
Record the review date and reviewer in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every critical operation's plan shows a review within the last 12 months, recorded in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Report the year's testing results to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Compile the year's test results, impact tolerance outcomes and remediation status into a summary report.
Present the summary via the board portal at the annual resilience review.
Record the committee's endorsement or required follow-up in the minutes.
checklist.done: the annual resilience summary is presented and the committee's response is recorded in the minutes.

checklist.step: Escalate any critical operation that cannot meet its impact tolerance
actions: For any operation with a persistent Failed classification, escalate to the Board Risk Committee with root cause and options (investment, process redesign, tolerance re-set).
Record the decision and its funding/owner in the GRC platform.
Track the decision to implementation.
checklist.done: every persistent Failed operation has an escalated, owned decision recorded and tracked.

checklist.step: Log any BCP/DR program exceptions
actions: Raise a tracker issue for any critical operation missing a current plan, an overdue test, or an unremediated Failed result.
Assign a root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Track the exception to closure in the regulatory filing/issue tracker.
checklist.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and remediation date logged.

checklist.step: Retain the BCP/DR evidence
actions: Move the plan, runbook, test scripts, results and after-action reports into the compliance evidence repository under the operation name.
Apply the 7-year-from-supersession retention label.
Confirm the repository index shows the record searchable by operation name and test date.
checklist.done: the BCP/DR record is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by operation name.

testing.step: Build the population of critical operations and their current-year tests
actions: Export the critical-operations list and the current-year test calendar from the GRC platform.
Reconcile the operation count to the business impact analysis module's approved list.
Resolve any discrepancy with the Business Continuity Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the approved BIA list and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every critical operation to a current plan and a completed test
actions: Match each operation to a plan reviewed within the last 12 months and a test completed within the fiscal year.
List any operation missing a current plan or a completed test as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every operation is matched to a current plan and test, or listed as an exception.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of operations with a Degraded or Failed test result.
Take a random sample of 8 remaining operations with a Met result, seeded and reproducible.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers every Degraded/Failed operation.

testing.step: Re-verify the test result classification for each sampled operation
actions: Open the raw test results and the recorded impact tolerance for each sampled operation.
Independently reclassify the result as Met/Degraded/Failed without viewing the recorded classification first.
Compare to the recorded classification; any difference is an exception.
testing.done: each sampled operation has an independent re-classification and a documented comparison.

testing.step: Verify remediation plans for sampled gaps
actions: For each sampled Degraded/Failed operation, confirm a remediation item exists with an owner and target date.
For Failed results, confirm CRO review is on file.
Flag any gap without a remediation item or required CRO review.
testing.done: every sampled gap has a verified remediation item and, where required, CRO review.

testing.step: Confirm plan and runbook currency
actions: Confirm the plan and DR runbook for each sampled operation reflect the current organizational structure, systems and vendors.
Check the plan's dependency mapping against the current application/vendor inventory.
Flag any stale reference (retired system, departed vendor, old org structure).
testing.done: plan and runbook currency is confirmed for every sampled operation, or staleness is flagged.

testing.step: Trace the after-action report to the recorded test evidence
actions: Pull the after-action report and the raw test log for each sampled operation.
Confirm the after-action report's conclusions are supported by the raw test data.
Capture the test log screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each after-action report is confirmed supported by its raw test data, captured as evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the annual review cadence and confirm reminders fired
actions: Recompute the 12-month review window independently from the last recorded review date for each sampled operation.
Compare to the tracked next-review date in the GRC platform.
Confirm the T-60/T-30/T-10 reminder alerts fired, using the platform's notification log.
testing.done: the recomputed review window matches the tracked date and reminders are confirmed fired.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the operation and what was missed.
Assign a root cause (stale plan, missed test, unremediated failure) and an owner.
Set a remediation date and carry open exceptions into next year's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance stale-plan and unmet-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and tested none of the sampled plans, sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board Risk Committee and file the workpaper in the evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and exception rate exists, reported to the Board Risk Committee.
